newsitem.title: UK: Pentland says Katy sale means one-off charge.
newsitem.headline: Pentland says Katy sale means one-off charge.

text.p: British clothing company Pentland Group Plc said on Tuesday that the sale of its U.S. unit Woods to Katy Industries Inc will result in an exceptional charge against its 1996 earnings.
Pentland, which earlier confirmed completion of the sale for $46 million in cash, said the proceeds woold be used to pay part of Woods' debt, which totals around $80 million.
The debt mainly consists of money owed to other parts of the Pentland Group and "will result in an exceptional charge being taken," Pentland said, without specifying the figure.
Finance director Frank Farrant told Reuters that the charge related to Woods would total 21 million stg.
But he added that the planned disposal of the remainder of the group's Consumer Products Division should even out the loss.
Pentland is in talks to sell its Hanson White greeting cards operation and the U.S. electronics specialist Holmes products. Farrant said, however, that neither agreement had yet been completed.

The sale of Woods, which makes and distributes electrical goods and components, and the other consumer products interests, is part of Pentlands' strategy of concentrating on its portfolio of sports and leisure brands.
